A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Decoding Game research. All 20 pages of each version, including equations, tables, Figure 1, and Appendices A–B, support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original text-generation evaluations in Table 1, parameter-sensitivity results in Tables 2–3, and a truncation case study in Figure 1.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results in Table 1 and Appendix B, including Tables 2–3 and Figure 1.

M1.justification: The Decoding Game formulation, local decoding strategy, objectives, and Game sampling procedure are unchanged. Algorithm 1 retains the same truncation, temperature scaling, normalization, and sampling steps.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same WebText open-ended continuation task and retain the same one-token and 35-token context scenarios in Appendix B.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains Nucleus, Contrastive, Typical, Basis-Aware (BA-η), Greedy, and Pure decoding as comparators for every model. Figure 1 retains the Game-versus-Nucleus comparison.

E3.justification: Both use 5,000 WebText test articles, 35-token prompts, a maximum generation length of 256 tokens, and the same six model configurations. Metrics, parameter settings, and selection by best MAUVE score remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix B retains the same epsilon/temperature sensitivity analyses in Tables 2–3 and the GPT-2 XL truncation case study in Figure 1. No analyses are added or removed.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same point-estimate results without repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Uncertainty-reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: All result entries in Tables 1–3 and both plots in Figure 1 are unchanged. For example, Game sampling's GPT-2 XL MAUVE score remains 0.958 in Table 1; reported rankings and parameter trends also match.

T1.justification: Sections 3–4 retain the same definitions, assumptions, propositions, theorems, and corollaries. Appendix A's proofs are unchanged; different equation page breaks introduce no mathematical revision.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about the minimax framework, implicit regularization, approximate optimality of heuristic sampling, objective generalization, and empirical support.

C2.justification: Interpretations of truncation, regularization, and parameter tradeoffs remain unchanged. Both retain the same discussion of computational intractability, local strategies, and extending the analysis beyond TV distance.

D1.justification: v3 adds a code-availability statement and repository address to the empirical-evidence bullet in Section 1.2. v2 lacks this implementation-access pointer; other technical disclosures are unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and reference entries are unchanged. Section 2 retains the same positioning relative to decoding theory, decision-making approaches, and robust optimization.

P1.justification: v3 shortens the opening sentence of Section 1.2, adds the code-access sentence, and removes the standalone title-page date. The section hierarchy and substantive narrative remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Paragraph indentation and spacing change, causing text and equation reflow. Algorithm 1 now precedes the complete evaluation description, and Table 1 precedes the start of the conclusion. Figure and table designs, labels, and captions remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The new implementation link in Section 1.2 provides a concrete access pointer, improving reproducibility guidance. The theory, experimental evidence, and appendix analyses are unchanged, so the overall quality gain is limited.
